correctness.rationale: The hyperboloid proof reduces every support width exactly to the largest Lorentz pairing of the support normal with a vertex. The inverse Gram matrix turns unit-normal normalization into a quadratic objective whose restriction to each required coordinate face is strictly convex. Therefore only zero-one patterns can minimize width; the exact consecutive-difference formula has the unique maximizing cardinality k=ceil(d/2), yielding both the formula and all equality cases.

originality.rationale: The motivating source defines Lassak thickness, computes facet width for regular simplices, and exhibits a narrower edge support for regular hyperbolic tetrahedra, but does not prove that edge support is globally minimizing or classify minimizers. Earlier equidistant-thickness work uses a different width notion, and later isominwidth work does not determine the regular-simplex thickness. Focused searches found no equivalent all-dimensional theorem.
residual_risks: Dekster's 2001 full text was not available through the inspected public publisher page; its abstract makes clear that it uses a different width notion, so it is not a decisive unresolved comparison, but it remains a terminology-related access risk.
The proof is short once the Lorentz Gram formulation is chosen, so an equivalent observation could exist in an unindexed note, thesis, or differently phrased discussion.
No claim is made for nonregular or ideal hyperbolic simplices or for other notions of hyperbolic width.

value.rationale: The motivating theory defines thickness as the central minimum-width invariant, while its canonical regular-simplex examples stop short of the global minimization. The exact formula and complete equality classification determine this invariant on the fundamental symmetric family in every dimension, reveal a parity-dependent minimizing face dimension, and upgrade the source's three-dimensional edge-support witness to the actual thickness.
